newsitem.title: GERMANY: SOCCER-MATTHAEUS SAYS KLINSMANN SHOULD MAKE UP HIS MIND.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-MATTHAEUS SAYS KLINSMANN SHOULD MAKE UP HIS MIND.

text.p: Bayern Munich captain Lothar Matthaeus said on Sunday it was time Juergen Klinsmann made up his mind whether he wanted to stay in Munich because the uncertainty was hurting the team.

In a column in the Bild am Sonntag newspaper, Matthaeus wrote: "We are all suffering when he says in November he is going to stay, then in December he says he wants to go and then in January it will be something else.
"In the team, the players keep asking: Is he staying? Is he going? Or is he going to stay afterall? I simply have to demand that he makes a clear decision."
Bayern president Franz Beckerbauer said on Saturday he expected Klinsmann to stay in Munich for the rest of the current Bundesliga season and beyond.
The German media has been filled with reports in recent weeks that Klinsmann wanted away from Bayern because of ill feeling between himself and team mates, in particular Matthaeus.
Klinsmann castigated his team in a recent television interview, accusing them of playing too cautiously.
Frustrated at scoring just five goals in 17 matches this season, Klinsmann threatened to leave at the end of the season unless they adopted a more attacking style.
Klinsmann said he respected Bayern coach Giovanni Trapattoni but said the Italian's defensive system made it difficult for strikers to operate.
Matthaeus, who earlier this year was left out of the German national team after he accused Klinsmann of undermining his position, criticised his team mate for questioning Trapattoni's tactics.
"Juergen Klinsmann has publicly complained about the tactics of our coach and that he doesn't get enough scoring opportunities from us," Matthaeus said.
"But in the last international match against Portugal, he had just one scoring chance 15 minutes before the end...," Matthaeus said.
"With Bayern Munich, he had an average of three scoring chances per match. I have to ask myself why he doesn't utter similar criticism (at the national team) after the match."
